preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 10^4 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 10**5 for n in (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: Each test case n is an integer between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line.split()) == n or output_line.strip() == '-1' for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either a permutation of length n or the string '-1'.

postconditions.expression: all(all(0 <= int(p_i) <= n-1 for p_i in output_line.split()) if output_line.strip() != '-1' else True for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])))
postconditions.description: If the output is a permutation, all elements are distinct integers in the range [0, n-1].

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(int(p_i) == j for j in range(n)) for p_i in output_line.split()) if output_line.strip() != '-1' else True for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])))
postconditions.description: If the output is a permutation, it contains all integers from 0 to n-1 exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(all(any((int(p_i) + i) == y**2 for y in range(int((int(p_i) + i)**0.5) + 1)) for i, p_i in enumerate(output_line.split())) if output_line.strip() != '-1' else True for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])))
postconditions.description: If the output is a permutation, for every index i, the value p_i + i is a perfect square.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line.strip() == '-1' or any(all(int(p_i) == j for j in range(n)) for p_i in output_line.split()) for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])))
postconditions.description: If a permutation exists, the output is that permutation; otherwise, the output is '-1'.
